display.title: The Baal Shem Tov and the Ten Wedding Gifts, Part 1
display.summary_short: Two orphans give away their wedding money to free a captive Jew. At their wedding a mysterious tzaddik and his ten students promise them ten gifts that belong to local noblemen.
display.summary_long: After a recent Siyum HaRambam, the storyteller explains why the Rebbe asked everyone to learn Rambam every day: it covers the whole Torah, unites all Jews in one study, and its 83 subjects of halachah protect against illness. He describes the three daily options the Rebbe gave. Since Shavuos, the Baal Shem Tov's yahrzeit, is coming, he tells a Baal Shem Tov story. Reuven, a generous innkeeper, takes in two orphans, Avraham and Sarah, arranges their marriage and gives them 600 gold coins to buy what they need. On the road they find an old Jew in chains and give every coin to free him. Reuven praises their mitzvah and gives them the money again. At the wedding a radiant tzaddik with ten students arrives, leads the chuppah and reveals that he is the Baal Shem Tov. Each student then 'gives' the couple something owned by a different poritz: the town, the lakes, the forests. How can this come true? To be continued. The program ends with a Yiddish song listing the fourteen books of the Rambam.
display.lesson: Saving a fellow Jew is worth everything we have, and Hashem rewards kindness in ways that are perfectly planned. Learn Rambam every day.
